title: finding(core): the `as ComponentMeta` cast PR #8297 removes is guarded only by a source-text pin — `<ComponentMeta>{…}`, a reformat, or a differently-spelled assertion all slip past it
body:
Observation-class finding, raised by the Clause-② contract review of PR #8297 (objectui#6950) and filed by the accepting seat. Unassigned, no labels — grading is the triage seat's.

## The claim

The #6950 ruling makes removing the `as ComponentMeta` cast a **deliverable**, on the stated ground that a cast hides subsequent shape drift. PR #8297 removes it and pins the removal — but the pin is a **source-text match** on `Registry.ts`, and a source-text match is the weakest guard available for this particular assertion.

Measured on `origin/main` = `8f9d87a`, the cast the ruling is about:

```
packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts:394
  return { ...(meta ?? {}), inputs: [...inputs, { ...ELEMENT_DATA_SOURCE_INPUT }] } as ComponentMeta;
```

(⚠️ The card #6950 cites `:313` and its triage comment cites other numbers — all stale. `:394` is the current coordinate.)

## Why a text pin is the wrong instrument here

The reviewer's reasoning, which I reproduce because it is the substance of the finding: **`tsc` cannot see this regression at all.** Re-adding the cast to the typed splice leaves `tsc --noEmit` at exit 0 — a type assertion is invisible to the compiler by construction. That is precisely why the author fell back to reading source text, and it is an honest fallback, not a lazy one.

But a text pin over source is:

- **formatting-brittle** — a line wrap, a prettier pass, or an intervening variable moves the matched string;
- **blind to the other spellings** — `<ComponentMeta>{…}` is the same assertion in angle-bracket form and would not match; nor would an assertion introduced on a different expression in the same function;
- **silent when it drifts** — a pin that stops matching what it was written to catch usually still passes, because it is asserting the absence of a string.

⇒ The guard passes today and would keep passing through the change it exists to prevent.

## The stronger instrument the review named

A scoped ESLint rule — `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-assertions` with `assertionStyle: 'never'` — applied to `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts`. That is AST-level, so it catches both spellings, survives reformatting, and fails loudly at the same gate the repo already runs (`Lint`). Whether the scope should be that one file, the registry directory, or something wider is the open question this card carries; ⛔ a repo-wide ban is a much larger decision and is NOT what this card proposes.

## Scope note

⛔ The ruling never required pinning the cast at all — the pin is the author's own addition, and it is better than nothing. This card is about upgrading a guard, not about a defect in PR #8297, and it should ⛔ not be read as a reason to hold that PR.

## Refs

- objectui#6950 / PR #8297 — the ruling, the removal, and the review that raised this (https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/6950#issuecomment-5568333150).
- A pre-existing sibling the same rule would surface, recorded not filed: `as unknown as RegistryConfigLike[]` in `gen-manifest.ts`.
